Five-part multi-step item covering 9.3, 9.5 and 9.9. It requires choosing the right relationship each time (ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, ΔG = −RT ln K, E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode, ΔG = −nFE). Part A uses the 188 J → 0.188 kJ conversion: ΔG = −112 − 500(−0.188) = −18 kJ.

Part B gives T = ΔH/ΔS = 596 K. Both ΔH and ΔS are negative, so the reaction is favorable below that temperature.

Part C uses K = exp(18000/(8.314·500)) = exp(4.33), about 76. This needs a calculator but only one step of arithmetic.

Part D has Zn as the anode and Fe as the cathode, with electrons flowing from Zn to Fe through the wire. E° = −0.44 − (−0.76) = 0.32 V.

Part E gives ΔG = −2(96485)(0.32) ≈ −62 kJ/mol, which is negative and therefore indicates a thermodynamically favorable reaction.

The reading load is modest. The bundle spans several topics and representation types, but none of the difficulty comes from unfair sources.
